about: Pool of randomised appearances for the 'random appearance' button of character creation (gui::DCCharacterCreation RandomAppearanceIndex/Count, HasNewRandomAppearance). Created by bg3.exe+0x2027B00 with 16 slots.

evidence.says: Creator bg3.exe+0x201D380 copies the 16-byte global DAT_14625AAD0 (a Guid that bg3.exe+0x2027B00 tests for all-zero, i.e. the null Guid) to +0..+0x10.

Same ring as RandomCharactersComponent, for appearances (Appearances at +0x18, size +0x24). EoCClient.dll DefinitionView::GetRandomAppearanceIndex (0x11BC4F0) shows (comp[+0x14] - comp[+0x10] - 1 + count) % count, and GetNextRandomAppearanceIndex (FUN_1811cc120) returns -1 when +0x14 equals +0x10: the slot of the most recently generated appearance. Creators write -1.

EoCClient.dll FUN_1811cc120 (GetNextRandomAppearanceIndex) starts from +0x14 and steps (mod the size at +0x24) to the next eoc::character_creation::Appearance slot; GetRandomAppearanceIndex (0x11BC4F0) shows its position relative to +0x10. The slot the shown random appearance is taken from.

Creator zeroes +0x18..+0x28; destructor bg3.exe+0x6ACFB0 resizes the array at +0x18 to 0 with bg3.exe+0x6DAAE0 (stride 0xD8) and frees it; bg3.exe+0x2027B00 resizes it to 16. macOS: ls::DynamicArray<eoc::character_creation::Appearance>::Reallocate(.., 0x10).

open_questions: Meaning of the Guid at +0 and of the 8 bytes at +0x10.
survey.second_pass: Not settled: all Windows users (bg3.exe+0x1F8A210, 0x208DA70, 0x208EB70, 0x20769F0) only fetch the component into view structures for the command processor; the reader of +0x10 (macOS ecl::character_creation::_private::ProcessCommands template, bg3_macos_x64+0x39DE7A0) has no matched Windows counterpart (decomp.py matches finds none), so the width of the 8 bytes at +0x10 is still open.
